links.outcome: Guideline-concordant recommendations when radiology inputs were deliberately erroneous or discordant with the exam
links.effect: Guided ChatGPT 30% strict accuracy (3/10) in mismatch cases; non-logged-in 60% (6/10). Error-aware prompts did not change recommendations.
links.quote: Even after being explicitly cautioned about possible examiner or measurement error, ChatGPT continued to recommend the same treatment strategies, failing to redirect toward repeat imaging or urgent consultation.

links.outcome: Recognition of discordant findings and deferral via repeat imaging or urgent pediatric orthopedic referral
links.effect: In mismatch scenarios ChatGPT frequently overtreated and failed to recommend repeat ultrasound or urgent referral, even when prompted with error-aware adjustments.
links.quote: The guided model achieved only 30% strict accuracy in these cases, often suggesting overtreatment such as early surgical intervention, while failing to recommend repeat ultrasound, second-reader confirmation, or urgent referral to a pediatric orthopedist.

links.outcome: Consistency of clinical recommendations between Swahili and English prompts
links.effect: Swahili outputs (translated back to English) were clinically identical to English outputs across concordant and mismatch cases.
links.quote: The translated outputs were clinically identical to the English versions across both concordant and mismatch cases, confirming language-independent consistency.

links.outcome: Concordance of LLM management recommendations with AAOS 2022 and AAP 2016 guidelines
links.effect: Concordant scenarios: guided 20/20 (100%) correct, non-logged-in 19/20 (95%). Mismatch scenarios: guided 3/10 correct, non-logged-in 6/10 correct.

links.outcome: Accuracy of LLM outputs against guideline reference standard, guided vs non-logged-in
links.effect: Concordant cases 100% (guided) vs 95% (non-logged-in); mismatch cases 30% vs 60% strict accuracy, 50% vs 80% including partially correct.
links.quote: Non-logged-in ChatGPT: Performed relatively better in this subgroup, with 60% strict accuracy (6/10 correct) and 80% if partially correct were included.

links.outcome: Need for human oversight given LLM errors in ambiguous cases
links.effect: ChatGPT overtreated or gave inappropriate recommendations without prompting for repeat imaging in mismatch cases; authors conclude human oversight is essential.
links.quote: This suggests that in real-world clinical environments, where measurement variability is frequent, ChatGPT should not be used without human oversight.

unlisted_practices: Guideline-based system prompting (instructing the model to follow AAOS/AAP guidelines) compared with unprompted use
